purpose: Manual forward evaluations of observable decisions; no exact wording assertions.

scenarios.name: swiftui-screen-review
scenarios.prompt: Review this SwiftUI product screen for VoiceOver and Dynamic Type. It uses icon-only buttons, a star rating built from tappable images, .font(.system(size: 14)) everywhere, and a promo carousel that auto-advances. Keep the visual design and the iOS 17 deployment target.
assess: Reports blocked tasks with element, file/line, and smallest fix
Makes the rating one adjustable element or an accessibilityRepresentation
Labels icon buttons by action and keeps SF Symbol defaults only when accurate
Moves text to text styles or relativeTo: fonts and reflows at accessibility sizes
Stops auto-advance under Reduce Motion or adds a pause control
Gates iOS 18+/26+ APIs and doesn't raise the deployment target

scenarios.name: custom-gesture-control
scenarios.prompt: Our drawing canvas zooms with pinch, pans with two fingers, and deletes strokes with a long press. Make it usable with VoiceOver, Switch Control, and Voice Control.
assess: Adds zoom action and named custom actions or menu commands for pan and delete
Considers direct touch with requiresActivation for drawing while keeping actions
Uses the SDK-valid accessibilityAction(named:) and accessibilityDirectTouch(options:)
Announces results without flooding speech
Lists device checks that remain

scenarios.name: nutrition-label-claim
scenarios.prompt: Can we claim VoiceOver, Larger Text, and Captions for our iPhone and Apple TV app? Sign-in uses a custom PIN pad, descriptions truncate at AX3, and only half the catalog has captions.
assess: Decides per device and feature against common tasks
Does not claim VoiceOver until the PIN pad works with VoiceOver
Withholds Larger Text while essential text truncates; notes tvOS 27 Large Text
Explains the caption-availability rule and CC badges
Mentions accuracy under App Review Guideline 2.3 and the accessibility URL

scenarios.name: uikit-carousel-modal
scenarios.prompt: In our UIKit app the favorite button is only reachable after swiping through every carousel item, and VoiceOver can reach views behind our custom photo overlay.
assess: Uses an adjustable carousel element returned from accessibilityElements with the buttons
Posts layout changes on scroll
Sets accessibilityViewIsModal and posts a screen change; supports escape
Doesn't replace the presentation architecture unnecessarily

scenarios.name: mac-pro-app
scenarios.prompt: Our SwiftUI Mac app has a 60-control inspector and actions that appear on hover. VoiceOver users say it takes forever to get around.
assess: Groups regions into labeled containers without deep nesting
Uses sort priority and rotors where scanning is visual
Exposes hover actions as actions plus keyboard shortcuts or visible controls
Notes Mac users' reliance on keyboard accelerators

scenarios.name: reading-app
scenarios.prompt: Our reader draws each page with Core Text and splits paragraphs into separate views. VoiceOver read-all stops at the end of each page and line navigation stops at each paragraph.
assess: Links paragraphs (text navigation elements or accessibilityLinkedGroup on iOS 27)
Adds causesPageTurn and accessibilityScroll with a page-scrolled announcement
Recommends UITextInput (or UIAccessibilityReadingContent) for drawn text
Puts selection actions in the edit rotor

scenarios.name: assistive-access
scenarios.prompt: Add Assistive Access support to our iOS 17+ photo app built with a UIKit app delegate.
assess: Chooses between the iOS 26 scene with UISupportsAssistiveAccess and full-screen mode with the correct keys
Uses an NSObject UIHostingSceneDelegate and the windowAssistiveAccessApplication role
Gates the scene for iOS 26
Applies the design principles: one or two tasks, icons with text, no hidden gestures or timers, guarded deletion

scenarios.name: visionos-realitykit
scenarios.prompt: Make our visionOS game's RealityKit targets accessible. Players hit them with a two-handed gesture, and the HUD follows the head.
assess: Adds AccessibilityComponent with label, value, traits, and activate action
Handles Direct Gesture mode with announcements
Provides alternatives to the two-handed gesture
Re-anchors the HUD when accessibilityPrefersHeadAnchorAlternative is true

scenarios.name: regression-testing
scenarios.prompt: Set up CI so accessibility doesn't regress in our iOS app.
assess: Adds performAccessibilityAudit with documented ignores and per-screen coverage
Uses accessibilityIdentifier rather than labels in tests
Considers the iOS 27 XCUIVoiceOverService with its beta caveats
States what automation can't verify

scenarios.name: media-player
scenarios.prompt: Our custom AVPlayerLayer player renders its own subtitles. Users say captions ignore their caption style and don't turn on automatically.
assess: Reads MediaAccessibility caption appearance and observes changes
Defaults captions from the system preference
Adds a selection UI and subtitle style preview where available (iOS 26.4)
Mentions generated subtitles in iOS 27 and audio descriptions

scenarios.name: discovery-boundary-web
scenarios.prompt: Audit our React marketing site for WCAG 2.2 AA.
assess: Doesn't apply Apple-platform API guidance to a web-only project beyond noting WebKit/VoiceOver testing

scenarios.name: discovery-boundary-unrelated
scenarios.prompt: Change the tint color of our app's Liquid Glass toolbar.
assess: Doesn't expand into an accessibility audit; at most notes contrast checks for the new tint
